title: Skid Buffer (Registered Ready)
constraints: A pipeline stage that breaks **both** the valid/data path and the ready path: `in_ready` must come straight from a register (`in_ready = !skid_valid`), with no combinational path from `out_ready`.

State: a main register (`out_valid`/`out_data`) and a skid register. On each edge: if the main register can advance (`!out_valid || out_ready`), it loads the skid entry if there is one (emptying the skid), otherwise it takes the input (`out_valid <= in_valid && in_ready`). If the main register is stalled, an accepted input goes into the skid register.
Full throughput (one transfer per cycle when `out_ready = 1`), no loss, no duplication. Synchronous reset empties both. `out_data` is don't-care while `out_valid = 0`.
hints: The skid register exists because `in_ready` is one cycle late: the upstream may already have sent a word in the cycle the output stalled.
Two valid bits, two data registers, and `in_ready = ~skid_valid`.
This is the standard way to pipeline a long ready path in AXI-Stream designs.

examples.title: streaming
examples.expected: one word per cycle, one cycle of latency

examples.title: skid
examples.expected: one word goes to the skid register, in_ready drops, nothing is lost
